content.title: About
content.content: Tomato soup in a can or carton is a ready‑to‑eat product made from ripe tomatoes, water, spices and a modest amount of salt. The reduced‑sodium version contains only 0.3 g of salt per 100 ml, making it suitable for people watching their sodium intake.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomato soup is one of the most popular ready‑made soups worldwide.
Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, a powerful antioxidant that gives the soup its bright red color.
Canning preserves nutrients for 2‑3 years without the need for artificial preservatives.
Sodium reduction is often achieved by replacing part of the salt with potassium‑based salt substitutes.
Tomato soup is frequently used as a base for more complex dishes such as stews or sauces.

items.title: High in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties, supports heart health and may lower the risk of certain cancers.

items.title: Reduced sodium
items.content: Lower salt content helps control blood pressure and reduces kidney strain.

items.title: Vitamins A and C
items.content: Tomatoes provide vitamins A and C, which support immunity and vision.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: A warm soup is easy on the stomach and promotes better nutrient absorption.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Being mostly water, the soup contributes to daily fluid intake.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes or added spices.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Certain brands may contain added sugar, which should be considered in low‑sugar diets.

items.title: BPA in packaging
items.content: Carton packages can be lined with BPA‑containing resins; choose BPA‑free labeled products.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Although reduced, sodium is still present; people on strict low‑sodium diets should count it toward their daily limit.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the soup in a pot or microwave until boiling, optionally stir in fresh herbs, cream, or croutons. It can also serve as a base for pasta, risotto, or be added to vegetable stews.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened can or carton in a cool, dry place. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and keep refrigerated for 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor or discoloration.
